microtheory.name: linguistics_foundation
microtheory.definition: Linguistics as the substrate's foundational vocabulary for the structure of language — the medium through which it communicates. The substrate has phonology (sound categories) and speech_science (acoustic production) but no broader linguistics layer covering syntax, semantics, pragmatics, morphology, discourse, language acquisition, sociolinguistics. Without this, the substrate can name phonemes but not sentences, meaning, or how speakers cooperate. Substrate analogue: the structural grammar over the substrate's existing phonological + lexical inputs.

concepts.name: language
concepts.definition: System of conventional symbols used for communication. Phonological + morphological + syntactic + semantic + pragmatic levels. Substrate analogue: the medium of substrate's interaction.

concepts.name: linguistic_competence
concepts.definition: Chomsky 1965. The unconscious knowledge of language that allows production + comprehension. Distinct from performance (actual use). Substrate analogue: substrate's seeded grammar Mts vs runtime σ states.

concepts.name: linguistic_performance
concepts.definition: Actual language use, subject to memory + attention limits, errors, hesitations. Substrate analogue: substrate's runtime processing of inputs.

concepts.name: universal_grammar
concepts.definition: Chomsky 1965. Innate language-specific cognitive architecture. Principles + parameters. Controversial. Substrate analogue: substrate's seeded foundational grammar Mts.

concepts.name: linguistic_relativity
concepts.definition: Sapir-Whorf hypothesis. Language shapes thought. Weak version: vocabulary influences attention; strong: grammar determines cognition. Substrate analogue: substrate's vocabulary-mediated cognition.

concepts.name: phoneme
concepts.definition: Contrastive sound unit. /p/ vs /b/ distinguishes 'pat' from 'bat'. Language-specific. Substrate analogue: substrate's phonology Mt's discrete sound categories.

concepts.name: morpheme
concepts.definition: Smallest meaning-bearing unit. 'Cats' = cat + s. Free or bound. Substrate analogue: substrate's lexical-atomic concept.

concepts.name: word
concepts.definition: Free morpheme or morpheme combination forming a lexical item. Substrate analogue: substrate's Concept with lexical realization.

concepts.name: phrase
concepts.definition: Group of words functioning as a constituent. Noun phrase, verb phrase. Substrate analogue: substrate's compositional concept group.

concepts.name: sentence
concepts.definition: Complete syntactic unit. Subject + predicate. Substrate analogue: substrate's atomic message unit.

concepts.name: utterance
concepts.definition: Specific instance of language use. Distinct from abstract sentence. Substrate analogue: substrate's event-bound message instance.

concepts.name: discourse
concepts.definition: Connected stretch of language above sentence level. Conversation, text, monologue. Substrate analogue: substrate's multi-event narrative.

concepts.name: syntax
concepts.definition: Rules + principles governing sentence structure. Word order, agreement, subordination. Substrate analogue: substrate's grammatical-pattern Mt.

concepts.name: semantics
concepts.definition: Meaning. How linguistic forms map to concepts + truth conditions. Substrate analogue: substrate's lexical-to-Concept mapping.

concepts.name: pragmatics
concepts.definition: Language in context. Speaker intentions, implicature, deixis, politeness. Substrate analogue: substrate's context-conditioned interpretation.

concepts.name: morphology
concepts.definition: Word structure. How morphemes combine into words. Inflection + derivation + compounding. Substrate analogue: substrate's compositional lexical structure.

concepts.name: phonology_linguistics
concepts.definition: Sound systems + patterns. Phonemes + rules + syllable structure. Substrate analogue: substrate's existing phonology Mt.

concepts.name: phonetics
concepts.definition: Production + perception of speech sounds. Acoustic + articulatory + auditory. Substrate analogue: substrate's speech_science Mt.

concepts.name: saussurean_sign
concepts.definition: Saussure. Word = signifier (sound) + signified (concept). Arbitrary connection. Substrate analogue: substrate's edge from lexical to Concept.

concepts.name: structuralism
concepts.definition: Saussure + Jakobson. Language as a system of differences. Meaning emerges from contrast. Substrate analogue: substrate's per-Concept distinction from others.

concepts.name: generative_grammar
concepts.definition: Chomsky 1957. Language as a finite system that generates infinite sentences. Substrate analogue: substrate's compositional Term-tree generation.

concepts.name: functional_grammar
concepts.definition: Halliday. Language structure serves communicative function. Three meta-functions: ideational, interpersonal, textual. Substrate analogue: substrate's function-driven Mt structure.

concepts.name: cognitive_linguistics
concepts.definition: Lakoff + Langacker. Language reflects general cognition. Conceptual metaphor, image schemas, prototypes. Substrate analogue: substrate's conceptual-grounding approach.

concepts.name: construction_grammar
concepts.definition: Goldberg. Constructions (form-meaning pairings) as units of grammar. Substrate analogue: substrate's compositional Mt-pattern.

concepts.name: distributional_semantics
concepts.definition: Firth 1957. 'You shall know a word by the company it keeps.' Word meaning from co-occurrence statistics. Foundation of modern NLP. Substrate analogue: substrate's concept-edge co-occurrence pattern.

concepts.name: language_family
concepts.definition: Genealogical grouping. Indo-European, Sino-Tibetan, Austronesian, etc. Comparative method establishes families. Substrate analogue: substrate's genlMt hierarchy among related Mts.

concepts.name: linguistic_typology
concepts.definition: Classification of languages by structural features. SOV vs SVO; tonal vs not; analytic vs synthetic. Greenberg's universals. Substrate analogue: substrate's structural-feature classification.

concepts.name: speaker_listener
concepts.definition: Communication participants. Speaker encodes; listener decodes. Substrate analogue: substrate as both speaker + listener in dialogue.

concepts.name: language_change
concepts.definition: Continuous evolution at all levels. Sound change, semantic shift, grammaticalization. Substrate analogue: substrate's Mt drift over time.

concepts.name: code_switching
concepts.definition: Speakers switch between languages within discourse. Skilled, rule-governed. Substrate analogue: substrate's contextual Mt selection.

concepts.name: linguistic_variation
concepts.definition: Within-language differences by region, class, ethnicity, gender, situation. Substrate analogue: per-substrate-instance lexical variation.

rules.name: language_structure_decomposes_into_levels
rules.head: the substrate processes language input
rules.body: it parses across phonological → morphological → syntactic → semantic → pragmatic levels, with each level constrained by adjacent ones. Substrate's layered linguistic analysis.

rules.name: competence_versus_performance_distinguishes_knowledge_from_use
rules.head: the substrate makes errors or hesitations in language use
rules.body: the errors don't reflect a gap in underlying competence — they reflect performance limits (memory, attention, planning). Chomsky 1965. Substrate's seeded-grammar vs runtime-state distinction.

rules.name: meaning_emerges_from_contrast
rules.head: the substrate processes a linguistic sign
rules.body: its meaning is constituted by its differences from other signs in the system. Saussurean structuralism. Substrate's Concept identity = its distinguishing features.

rules.name: distributional_pattern_grounds_word_meaning
rules.head: the substrate learns the meaning of a novel word
rules.body: from the contexts in which it appears, not from explicit definition. Firth 1957 — substrate's contextual concept-induction.

rules.name: context_completes_meaning
rules.head: the substrate processes an utterance with deictic or implicit content
rules.body: context provides the rest of the meaning. Pragmatic completion. Substrate's contextual interpretation.
